docs.title: About
docs.text: The rbxcloud CLI and library is built for easy access into the Roblox Open Cloud APIs. The CLI can be used by developers and CD pipelines for external deployments, messaging, and datastore management. The Rust library can be used to build tools and applications on top of Roblox's Open Cloud APIs with ease.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
For documentation on the CLI, start on the CLI Installation page.

For documentation on the Rust library, start on the Rust Library Installation page.

docs.title: API Key
docs.text:
rbxcloud requires a Roblox API key to function. These keys can be created and managed on the Credentials Roblox page. Remember to always keep these keys secret.

Roblox API keys will auto-expire if not used for over 60 days. Use the Credentials page to regenerate the key if this occurs.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
As a general rule of practice for any API key:

  • Use the least number of permissions as needed
  • Keep the key in a secret location (e.g. GitHub Secrets, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.)
  • Never commit a key to a source code repository
  • Use as strict of a CIDR as possible
  • Use an expiration date to force periodic key rollovers (must be manually regenerated)

docs.title: Handling Compromised Keys
docs.text: If a key is suspected to have been compromised, use the Credentials page to immediately invalidate the key. This can be done by regenerating or deleting the key. Keys can also be disabled, but re-enabling the key will not change the key, thus is not a safe option to protect from a compromised key. If in doubt, regenerate the key.

docs.title: Storing Keys
docs.text:
There are many tools that can be used to securely store a key. GitHub has a Secrets page for each repository, which can then be used by GitHub Actions securely. AWS and GCP have a Secrets Manager service. Azure has the Key Vault service.

If a key must be located within a local repository's directory, be sure to add it to the .gitignore file. This is common in some .env file setups.

docs.title: Environment Variable
docs.text:
All CLI commands expect the --api-key parameter, but can also be set via the RBXCLOUD_API_KEY environment variable. With the environment variable set, the --api-key parameter can be left out.

To keep the key out of screenshots and CI logs, --help lists which environment variables each option reads but not their values:

$ rbxcloud datastore list-stores --help
  -a, --api-key <API_KEY>
          Roblox Open Cloud API Key [env: RBXCLOUD_API_KEY]

To check what is currently set, pass the global --show-env-values flag to any command, or set RBXCLOUD_SHOW_ENV_VALUES=true:

$ rbxcloud datastore list-stores --show-env-values --help
  -a, --api-key <API_KEY>
          Roblox Open Cloud API Key [env: RBXCLOUD_API_KEY=<your key>]

docs.title: Assets API
docs.text: Upload and manage assets, their versions, and who may use them.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
Create an asset 

Usage: rbxcloud assets create [OPTIONS] --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME> --description <DESCRIPTION> --creator-id <CREATOR_ID> --creator-type <CREATOR_TYPE> --filepath <FILEPATH> --api-key <API_KEY>

Options:
  -t, --asset-type <ASSET_TYPE>
          Asset type [possible values: audio-mp3, audio-ogg, audio-flac, audio-wav, decal-png, decal-jpeg, decal-bmp, decal-tga, model-fbx]
  -n, --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
          Display name
  -d, --description <DESCRIPTION>
          Description
  -e, --expected-price <EXPECTED_PRICE>
          Expected Robux price
  -i, --creator-id <CREATOR_ID>
          Creator ID
  -c, --creator-type <CREATOR_TYPE>
          Creator type [possible values: user, group]
  -f, --filepath <FILEPATH>
          File (full or relative path)
  -p, --pretty
          Pretty-print the JSON response
  -a, --api-key <API_KEY>
          Roblox Open Cloud API Key [env: RBXCLOUD_API_KEY]
      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Maximum seconds to wait for each request to Roblox (0 = no limit) [env: RBXCLOUD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT] [default: 120]
      --proxy <PROXY>
          Proxy URL for all requests (e.g. http://host:port or socks5://host:port). Defaults to the HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY environment variables [env: RBXCLOUD_PROXY]
      --show-env-values
          Show environment variable values (e.g. API keys) in help output. Hidden by default to avoid leaking secrets [env: RBXCLOUD_SHOW_ENV_VALUES]
  -h, --help
          Print help

Example: 

$ rbxcloud assets create -t decal-png -n Logo -d "Game logo" -c user -i 156 -f logo.png -a MY_KEY

docs.title: Grant Permission
docs.text:
Grant a user, group, or experience permission to use or edit assets 

Usage: rbxcloud assets grant-permission [OPTIONS] --asset-ids <ASSET_IDS> --subject-type <SUBJECT_TYPE> --subject-id <SUBJECT_ID> --api-key <API_KEY>

Options:
  -i, --asset-ids <ASSET_IDS>
          Asset IDs (repeat or comma-separate)

  -t, --subject-type <SUBJECT_TYPE>
          Type of subject receiving access

          [possible values: user, group, universe]

  -s, --subject-id <SUBJECT_ID>
          ID of the user, group, or universe receiving access

  -g, --action <ACTION>
          Permission to grant

          [default: use]

          Possible values:
          - use:  Use the asset in experiences (e.g. audio, animations, models)
          - edit: Edit and manage the asset

  -d, --dependencies
          Also grant access to the assets' dependencies

  -p, --pretty
          Pretty-print the JSON response

  -a, --api-key <API_KEY>
          Roblox Open Cloud API Key

          [env: RBXCLOUD_API_KEY]

      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Maximum seconds to wait for each request to Roblox (0 = no limit)

          [env: RBXCLOUD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT]
          [default: 120]

      --proxy <PROXY>
          Proxy URL for all requests (e.g. http://host:port or socks5://host:port). Defaults to the HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY environment variables

          [env: RBXCLOUD_PROXY]

      --show-env-values
          Show environment variable values (e.g. API keys) in help output. Hidden by default to avoid leaking secrets

          [env: RBXCLOUD_SHOW_ENV_VALUES]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Example: 

$ rbxcloud assets grant-permission -i 111,222 -t universe -s 12345 -a MY_KEY

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
A common practice is to create a CD pipeline to deploy a place automatically. This can be done with GitHub actions. Below is an example GitHub Action workflow. The example assumes that Aftman is being used and that rbxcloud is listed within the aftman.toml file.

# Deploy any time code is pushed to the 'main' branch
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Aftman
        uses: ok-nick/setup-aftman@v0

      - name: Publish
        shell: bash
        env:
          UID: 123456789              # Universe ID
          PID: 123456789              # Place ID
          API_KEY: ${{ secrets.key }} # API Key (keep this in your GitHub Repository Secrets)
          FILE: my_place.rbxl         # Roblox place file (e.g. might have a step before this to build the file with Rojo)

        run: rbxcloud experience publish -a "$API_KEY" -u "$UID" -i "$PID" -t published -f "$FILE"

docs.title: Install CLI
docs.text: There are a few different ways to install the rbxcloud CLI.

docs.title: mise-en-place (Preferred)
docs.text:
Run mise use within your project directory. This adds rbxcloud to the project's mise.toml file (creating it if needed) and installs it from the GitHub releases. 

$ mise use github:Stinson-Moss/rbxcloud@0.19.0

Omit the version (github:Stinson-Moss/rbxcloud) to use the latest release. Anyone else working in the project then only needs to run mise install.

docs.title: Aftman
docs.text:
Run the aftman add command within your project directory. This will add rbxcloud to the project's aftman.toml file (or create one if it doesn't yet exist). 

$ aftman add Stinson-Moss/rbxcloud@0.19.0

Next, run aftman install to install rbxcloud.

docs.title: Foreman
docs.text:
Add rbxcloud under the [tools] section of your foreman.toml file. 

# foreman.toml
[tools]
rbxcloud = { github = "Stinson-Moss/rbxcloud", version = "0.19.0" }

Next, run foreman install to install rbxcloud.

Legacy

mise is preferred over Aftman and Foreman. For more information, see the mise-en-place documentation.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
A few prebuilt binaries are compiled and attached to each release.

  1. Go to the releases page
  2. Navigate to the desired version (e.g. the latest version)
  3. Download and unzip the desired executable
  4. Relocate the executable to a more permanent place
  5. Change your OS path variable to point to the executable

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the tool with the --version flag to verify the installation succeeded. 

$ rbxcloud --version

docs.title: HTTP Configuration
docs.text:
Every request goes through a shared HttpClient, which holds the API key, a connection pool, and the timeout and proxy settings. Client::new (v2) and RbxCloud::new (v1) create one with default settings:

Setting Default Total request timeout 120 seconds Connect timeout 30 seconds Proxy HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY environment variables

docs.title: Custom settings
docs.text:
Build an HttpClient and pass it to with_http:

use std::time::Duration;
use rbxcloud::{http::HttpClient, v2::Client};

let http = HttpClient::builder("API_KEY")
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
    .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
    .proxy("http://user:pass@proxy.local:8080")
    .build()?;

let client = Client::with_http(http.clone());
let legacy = rbxcloud::v1::RbxCloud::with_http(http);

Builder options:

  • timeout(Duration) / no_timeout()
  • connect_timeout(Duration)
  • proxy(url): supports http://, https://, and socks5:// URLs
  • no_proxy(): ignore proxy environment variables
  • user_agent(String)

An existing reqwest::Client can also be wrapped with HttpClient::from_reqwest(api_key, client).

docs.text:
The CLI exposes the same settings as global flags, available on every command:

--request-timeout <SECONDS>   Maximum seconds to wait for each request (0 = no limit) [env: RBXCLOUD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT] [default: 120]
--proxy <PROXY>               Proxy URL for all requests [env: RBXCLOUD_PROXY]
